sections.head: More ways to test agent-written code

items.q: How does a coding agent use Kane CLI?
items.a: The agent calls kane-cli run with a plain-English check after changing code. Kane CLI drives a real browser and returns an exit code and an evidence file.
Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor and Copilot can call Kane CLI from their terminal.

items.q: Does every run call an LLM?
items.a: No. The first run works out the path. When you save it as a test, its unchanged steps replay from cache with no LLM cost; a step that broke because the page changed is re-authored.

items.q: What does Kane CLI cost for agent use?
items.a: Kane CLI is free to install. Runs use KaneAI credits; you can claim 10,000 free Kane CLI credits valid for 30 days.

items.q: How is this different from a browser tool for agents?
items.a: A browser tool lets an agent act on a page. Kane CLI verifies the change against acceptance criteria and returns a verdict with evidence.
